claims.text: The baseline is a conventionally processed FeNiCrCoCu high-entropy-alloy coating on a conventional metal substrate.
Processing parameters or thermal treatments can be adjusted to produce a controlled grain-size refinement relative to the baseline coating.
Grain refinement increases the grain-boundary area or density in the coating.
Grain-size refinement enhances the high-temperature wear resistance of the FeNiCrCoCu coating.
Grain-size refinement promotes more homogeneous microscopic plastic deformation during sliding.
An increased density of refined grain boundaries facilitates dynamic recrystallization.
An increased density of refined grain boundaries enhances thermally activated grain-boundary sliding.
Dynamic recrystallization and grain-boundary sliding produce a more homogeneous distribution of deformation.
Dynamic recrystallization and grain-boundary sliding reduce stress-concentration sites.
At elevated temperature, refined grains distribute plastic strain more evenly.
More evenly distributed plastic strain retards the formation of localized deformation zones.
Localized deformation zones lead to accelerated wear.
Temperatures above approximately 500°C are near the service limit of the FeNiCrCoCu coating.
Above approximately 500°C, grain-boundary sliding and dynamic recrystallization become significant deformation mechanisms in the coating.
Under high-temperature sliding, the refined-grain coating will have a lower wear rate than the baseline coating.
Under high-temperature sliding, the refined-grain coating will exhibit less localized microscopic plastic deformation than the baseline coating.
